results.content: The tool consisted of a copper anode and monitored at kα wavelength of 0.15406 nm. ... The peaks corresponding to SBT AgNPs 2θ were found to be at 38.3°, 40.8°, 64.5°, 74.2°. The hkl planes at (111), (200), (220), and (311). ... The output from the XRD analysis affirmed that the AgNPs formed were FCC crystalline structure nanoparticles, in which the (111) hkl peak is the most dominant. [Model: Bragg's law $\lambda = 2d\sin\theta$ with the cubic spacing $d_{hkl} = a/\sqrt{h^2+k^2+l^2}$ gives $a = \lambda\sqrt{N}/(2\sin\theta)$, $N = h^2+k^2+l^2$. A single FCC phase requires every indexed peak to return the same lattice parameter $a$.]
results.route_rationale: Bragg's law plus cubic indexing is a crisp quantitative model; consistency of the four (2θ, hkl) pairs is formalisable.

lean_result.reasoning: Lean proved the **negation** of the FCC-consistency condition for the first two peaks. Eliminating $a$ between $a = \lambda\sqrt{3}/(2\sin\theta_1)$ for the $(111)$ peak at $2\theta = 38.3^\circ$ and $a = \lambda\sqrt{4}/(2\sin\theta_2)$ for the $(200)$ peak at $2\theta = 40.8^\circ$ requires $\sqrt{3}\sin 20.4^\circ = 2\sin 19.15^\circ$. The compiled theorem establishes the strict inequality $\sqrt{3}\sin(40.8\pi/360) < 2\sin(38.3\pi/360)$, using Mathlib's $\pi$ enclosure (`Real.pi_gt_d6`/`Real.pi_lt_d6`) and the Taylor bounds $x - x^3/6 < \sin x < x$ (`Real.sin_gt_sub_cube`, `Real.sin_lt`). Numerically the two peaks imply $a = 0.4066$ nm and $a = 0.4419$ nm — an $8.7\%$ mismatch, so they cannot be the $(111)$ and $(200)$ reflections of one cubic lattice. Outside the formal proof (bounds too loose to settle in Lean), the same arithmetic puts the fourth peak at odds too: $74.2^\circ$ read as $(311)$ gives $a = 0.4236$ nm, whereas JCPDS 04-0783 places Ag $(200)$ at $44.3^\circ$ and $(311)$ at $77.4^\circ$, not $40.8^\circ$ and $74.2^\circ$. The $(111)$ and $(220)$ peaks ($38.3^\circ$, $64.5^\circ$) are mutually consistent at $a \approx 0.4066$–$0.4084$ nm.

private lemma sin_enclosure {x lo hi : ℝ} (h0 : 0 < lo) (h1 : lo ≤ x) (h2 : x ≤ hi) :
    lo - hi ^ 3 / 6 < Real.sin x ∧ Real.sin x < hi := by
  have hx : 0 < x := lt_of_lt_of_le h0 h1
  refine ⟨?_, lt_of_lt_of_le (Real.sin_lt hx) h2⟩
  have hcube := Real.sin_gt_sub_cube hx
  nlinarith [pow_le_pow_left₀ hx.le h2 3, pow_pos hx 3]

theorem sbt_xrd_111_200_inconsistent :
    Real.sqrt 3 * Real.sin (40.8 * π / 360) < 2 * Real.sin (38.3 * π / 360) := by
  have hpl : π < 3.141593 := Real.pi_lt_d6
  have hpg : (3.141592 : ℝ) < π := Real.pi_gt_d6
  have h1 : (0.33423 : ℝ) ≤ 38.3 * π / 360 := by nlinarith
  have h1' : 38.3 * π / 360 ≤ (0.3342306 : ℝ) := by nlinarith
  have h2 : (0.3560470 : ℝ) ≤ 40.8 * π / 360 := by nlinarith
  have h2' : 40.8 * π / 360 ≤ (0.3560473 : ℝ) := by nlinarith
  obtain ⟨hs1, -⟩ := sin_enclosure (by norm_num) h1 h1'
  obtain ⟨hs2lo, hs2⟩ := sin_enclosure (by norm_num) h2 h2'
  have hr : Real.sqrt 3 < 1.7320509 := by
    rw [Real.sqrt_lt' (by norm_num)]; norm_num
  have hs2pos : 0 < Real.sin (40.8 * π / 360) := by
    have h : (0 : ℝ) < 0.3560470 - 0.3560473 ^ 3 / 6 := by norm_num
    linarith
  calc Real.sqrt 3 * Real.sin (40.8 * π / 360)
      < 1.7320509 * 0.3560473 :=
        mul_lt_mul' hr.le hs2 hs2pos.le (by norm_num)
    _ < 2 * (0.33423 - 0.3342306 ^ 3 / 6) := by norm_num
    _ < 2 * Real.sin (38.3 * π / 360) := by linarith

results.content: The peaks representing the chemically synthesized AgNPs appeared at 38.1°, 44.3°, 64.4°, 81.5°. The hkl planes relating to respective peaks were determined to (111), (200), (220), and (311) according to the data from Ref: Joint Committee on Powder Diffraction Standards, JCPDS file No. 04-0783. [With $\lambda = 0.15406$ nm and $a = \lambda\sqrt{N}/(2\sin\theta)$, one FCC phase requires all four peaks to return the same $a$.]

Numerically $(111)$ at $38.1^\circ$ gives $a = 0.40877$ nm while $81.5^\circ$ read as $(311)$ gives $a = 0.39138$ nm. The correct index is $(222)$, $N = 12$, which returns $a = 0.40879$ nm — matching the other three peaks ($a = 0.40877$, $0.40861$, $0.40886$ nm for $(111)$, $(200)$, $(220)$) to four decimal places. So this sample *is* a clean FCC silver phase; only the label on the fourth peak is wrong. JCPDS 04-0783 places Ag $(311)$ at $2\theta \approx 77.4^\circ$ and $(222)$ at $81.5^\circ$, confirming the mis-indexing.

def EquallySpaced (c : List ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j, i + 1 < c.length → j + 1 < c.length →
    c.getD (i + 1) 0 - c.getD i 0 = c.getD (j + 1) 0 - c.getD j 0

theorem mb_standard_series_not_equally_spaced :
    ¬ EquallySpaced [(0.05 : ℝ), 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3] ∧
      EquallySpaced [(0.05 : ℝ), 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3] := by

  · intro h
    have := h 0 1 (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
    norm_num [List.getD] at this
  · intro i j hi hj
    have hi' : i < 5 := by simp at hi; omega
    have hj' : j < 5 := by simp at hj; omega
    interval_cases i <;> interval_cases j <;> norm_num [List.getD]

results.content: The degradation activity was examined by photocatalytic removal of methylene blue and malachite green dyes from textile wastewater. The textile wastewater showed a decrease of methylene blue by 25% and 58.3%. The malachite green was also reduced by 33.3% and 60%, which was remarkably significant owing to the presence of the complex factor in the natural environment. [Results section: in textile wastewater malachite green fell 2.3 → 1.6 → 1.3 OD, i.e. 30.43% and 43.47%; the 33.3% and 60% figures come from the *pure* malachite green standard, 0.75 → 0.5 → 0.3 OD.]

verify_math_result.reasoning: The two methylene-blue figures are right: $25\%$ and $58.3\%$ are exactly the textile-wastewater values ($1.2 \to 0.9 \to 0.5$ OD), independently confirmed by the Lean check on `paper::FORMULA_BLOCK::1` and by the Fig. 10 bar graph. The malachite-green figures are not. For textile wastewater the Results section gives $2.3 \to 1.6$ OD in room light and $2.3 \to 1.3$ in sunlight, i.e. $30.43\%$ and $43.47\%$ (Lean-verified in `paper::FORMULA_BLOCK::0`, and reproduced in the manuscript's own Fig. 10 legend). The abstract's $33.3\%$ and $60\%$ are the *pure malachite green standard* values ($0.75 \to 0.5 \to 0.3$ OD, Lean-verified in `paper::FORMULA_BLOCK::3`), a different experiment on lab-prepared dye. Attributing them to "the textile wastewater" overstates sunlight removal of malachite green from wastewater by $16.5$ percentage points, and it inverts the paper's own argument — the discussion stresses that wastewater performance is lower because of "the complex factor in the natural environment", yet the abstract quotes the higher standard-solution numbers as the wastewater result.

results.location: Results and discussion — Zeta potential analysis
results.content: In this study, the observed zeta potential was -13.6 mV for chemically synthesized AgNPs (Fig. 7b) and SBT-AgNPs (Fig. 7a) were observed to be -17.5 mV with zeta deviation of 10.8 and -13.7 mV indicating the stability of silver nanoparticle suspension. ... It has been reported that low absolute zeta potential values lead to aggregation and flocculation due to the absence of repulsive force (Cataldo, 2014). Thus, the zeta potential SBT-AgNPs of -17.5 mv was found to repel each other and prevent aggregates ensuring long term stability.
results.route_rationale: Turns on instrument semantics the paper never pins down (what the two "deviation" numbers refer to), so a faithful formal statement is not available.

verify_math_result.reasoning: Two problems. First, a zeta deviation is the standard deviation of the measured zeta-potential distribution and is non-negative by construction, so the quoted "zeta deviation of 10.8 and -13.7 mV" cannot both be deviations — $-13.7$ mV is outside the range of the quantity. Nor is $-13.7$ reconcilable with the stated means: the chemically synthesised sample is $-13.6$ mV and the SBT sample $-17.5$ mV, and the abstract reports only $-17.5$ mV, so the third value is unexplained. Second, the stability inference is self-defeating against the paper's own criterion: it cites that "low absolute zeta potential values lead to aggregation", and $|-17.5|$ mV is low on the conventional scale (colloidal stability is usually taken to require $|\zeta| \gtrsim 30$ mV) — the same discussion in fact calls it "moderate colloidal stability" two sentences earlier. Concluding "long term stability" from $-17.5$ mV therefore does not follow from the stated premise. The sentence is garbled enough that a benign reading exists (e.g. "deviation 10.8" for one sample and a mistyped mean for the other), which is why this is reported at moderate rather than high confidence.

results.location: Results and discussion — The optimization of reaction time for the synthesis of SBT-AgNPs
results.content: The Fig. 3 associated with the SBT-AgNPs exhibited dome shaped peaks at 425 nm with the peaks associated with time period of 30, 60 and 90 min suitable for study while the peak linked with 120 min was abandoned owed to disruptions in its dome. The peak linked with 90 min has an absorption density of 2.9 while the peak of 60 min has ascent rise of 2.6. The ascent of 60 min peak showed a clear mark of 1.2 as compared to the peak associated with 30 min time. The mark was significantly reduced from 60 min peak to 90 min peak. Thus, it can be safely assumed that 60 min time was more efficient than the 90 min reaction time in spent black tea mediated synthesis of AgNPs. ... However, after 120 min the enhanced contact time showed the noise and junk in the peaks corresponding to the 90 and 120 min.
results.route_rationale: The load-bearing step rests on an undefined notion of "efficient"; no faithful formal statement exists.

verify_math_result.reasoning: The arithmetic is internally consistent: with $\mathrm{OD}(60) = 2.6$ and a "mark" of $1.2$ over the 30 min peak, $\mathrm{OD}(30) = 1.4$; the $60 \to 90$ increment is $2.9 - 2.6 = 0.3$, which is indeed "significantly reduced" relative to $1.2$. Two defects sit on top of it. (i) The inference does not follow: on the paper's own proxy for yield, $90$ min gives strictly more product than $60$ min ($2.9 > 2.6$), so "60 min time was more efficient than the 90 min reaction time" holds only under a yield-per-unit-time reading of "efficient" that the paper never defines; as written it asserts diminishing marginal return and concludes lower absolute yield. (ii) The passage contradicts itself about the 90 min peak: it is first listed among the peaks "suitable for study" (only 120 min being "abandoned owed to disruptions in its dome"), and later said to show "noise and junk". The trailing clause is also temporally incoherent — effects "after 120 min" cannot manifest in the 90 min spectrum.

findings.evidence: Lean proved $\sqrt{3}\,\sin(40.8\pi/360) < 2\,\sin(38.3\pi/360)$, i.e. the FCC-consistency condition $\sqrt{3}\sin\theta_{200} = 2\sin\theta_{111}$ **fails** for the paper's first two SBT-AgNP peaks. Bragg's law with the cubic spacing $d_{hkl} = a/\sqrt{h^2+k^2+l^2}$ gives $a = \lambda\sqrt{N}/(2\sin\theta)$, so $2\theta = 38.3^\circ$ as $(111)$ implies $a = 0.4066$ nm while $2\theta = 40.8^\circ$ as $(200)$ implies $a = 0.4419$ nm — an $8.7\%$ mismatch, impossible for a single phase. The fourth peak fails too (not formalised, bounds too loose): $74.2^\circ$ as $(311)$ gives $a = 0.4236$ nm. JCPDS 04-0783 places Ag $(200)$ at $44.3^\circ$ and $(311)$ at $77.4^\circ$ — the values the paper's own chemically synthesised control reports. The abstract-level claim that these four angles establish an FCC phase for SBT-AgNPs is therefore not supported by its own numbers.

The companion room-light figure is also slightly off — $16.67\%$ reported as $16\%$ — but that is within unit-digit truncation. summary:
Fifteen self-contained quantitative objects were extracted from this photocatalysis paper. It contains no display equations, theorems or proofs, so the mathematics worth checking is the arithmetic and the physical models behind the reported numbers: degradation percentages computed from stated absorbances, XRD peak indexing via Bragg's law, concentration/mass-balance bookkeeping, and the optimisation comparatives.

Ten snippets were routed to Lean and all ten returned a verdict — three `PASSED`, seven `REFUTED`, none `FAILED` or `NOT_ATTEMPTED`, so no informal fallbacks were needed. Five further snippets whose content is attribution, instrument semantics or prose inference went to informal review.

**What Lean settled.** Clean: the degradation percentages for malachite green in wastewater ($30.43\%$, $43.47\%$ from $2.3 \to 1.6 \to 1.3$ OD), for methylene blue in wastewater ($25\%$, $58.3\%$ from $1.2 \to 0.9 \to 0.5$ OD), and for the pure malachite-green standard ($33.3\%$, $60\%$ from $0.75 \to 0.5 \to 0.3$ OD) all reproduce exactly under $D = (A_0-A_f)/A_0 \times 100$. Refuted, each by a compiling proof of the negation:
1. **XRD indexing of SBT-AgNPs** (critical). Eliminating the lattice parameter between $a = \lambda\sqrt{N}/(2\sin\theta)$ for the $(111)$ peak at $38.3^\circ$ and the $(200)$ peak at $40.8^\circ$ requires $\sqrt{3}\sin 20.4^\circ = 2\sin 19.15^\circ$; Lean proved the strict inequality instead. The two peaks imply $a = 0.4066$ nm and $a = 0.4419$ nm, so they cannot belong to one FCC phase, and the abstract-level FCC claim for SBT-AgNPs is unsupported by its own angles.
2. **Pure methylene-blue sunlight degradation.** The stated absorbances give $38.89\%$, not the reported $35\%$.
3. **XRD indexing of the chemical control.** $81.5^\circ$ is the $(222)$ reflection ($a = 0.40879$ nm, matching the other three peaks), not $(311)$ ($a = 0.39138$ nm).
4. **Salt-optimisation comparative.** $2.35 < 2.8$, so 50 mM gave less absorption than 100 mM, not "comparatively more" — as the same paragraph's "highest absorption signal of 2.8" already implies.
5. **Methylene-blue standard series.** $0.05, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3$ mg is not equally spaced; the Methods section's $0.05 \ldots 0.3$ mg series is, so the two sections describe different experiments.
6-7. **Concentration bookkeeping.** With the dilution bound $c_s v_s/v_t \le c_s$ (proved), a $0.05$ mg/ml ($= 50$ mg/L) methylene-blue working solution is unreachable from a $30$ mg/L stock, and every malachite-green standard ($10$–$50$ g/L as stated) is unreachable from a $1$ g/L stock; the malachite-green working solution is also quoted both as $0.1$ and as $100$ mg/ml.

**What informal review added.** The abstract reports malachite-green removal from textile wastewater as $33.3\%$ and $60\%$, but those are the pure-standard figures; the wastewater values are $30.43\%$ and $43.47\%$ — a $16.5$ pp overstatement of the paper's headline result, and the only other critical finding. The conclusion compounds it by crediting malachite green's $43.47\%$ to methylene blue. Three lower-confidence issues: a negative "zeta deviation" ($-13.7$ mV) alongside a stability conclusion that contradicts the paper's own cited $|\zeta|$ criterion; "4 peaks" followed by three wavelengths; and the 60-vs-90 min efficiency inference, which contradicts the higher 90 min absorbance and the passage's own description of the 90 min spectrum.

**Agreement.** The two verifiers never disagreed — they examined disjoint snippets, and where they touch the same numbers (the four degradation series) the informal attribution findings rest on the Lean-verified arithmetic rather than contesting it.

**Verdict: CRITICAL_ERRORS**, at confidence $0.9$. Two confident critical findings — the SBT-AgNP FCC indexing (machine-refuted) and the abstract's misattributed malachite-green wastewater figures — both bearing on abstract-level claims, plus ten minor findings. Confidence is high because seven of the twelve findings are compiling refutations with no `sorryAx` and only the standard Mathlib axioms, and because no Lean run came back `FAILED`, so nothing was left unsettled for want of proof. The residual doubt is interpretive rather than formal: several refuted items read like unit or labelling slips, which is why they are graded minor.

**Lean project.** `MATH_VERIFICATION/Paper` was reused, not created — it is the shared project every `paper.md` run resolves to and holds other papers' saved proofs — so per the skill's reuse rule it was kept (`lean_project_kept: true`). The ten proofs are saved as `Paper/Verified/paper__<TYPE>__<i>_0009opus5.lean`; `TMP.lean` and `claim.md` scratch were removed.
